label: def:categorical-mordell-weil
title: Categorical Mordell--Weil group, $q$-Tate--Shafarevich group, and $q$-deformed $L$-function
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be a QOU with substrate parameter q and Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q (Descartes elliptic curve).

The categorical Mordell--Weil group is the abelian group of \mathbf{1}-rational points

\mathcal{E}_q(\mathbf{1}) := \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, E_q),

where E_q \in \mathrm{Ob}(\mathbf{C}) is the object whose fibre functor image \tau(E_q) = H^1(\mathcal{E}_q, \mathbb{Z}) is the first cohomology of the elliptic fiber. The group law is induced by chord-tangent addition on \mathcal{E}_q. Set r_q := \mathrm{rank}\,\mathcal{E}_q(\mathbf{1}). The Tannaka--Krein equivalence (reconstruction) identifies \mathbf{C} \simeq \mathrm{Rep}(G), giving

\mathcal{E}_q(\mathbf{1}) \cong \tau(E_q)^G = H^1(\mathcal{E}_q)^G.

We define r_q as the multiplicity of the trivial representation \mathbf{1} in the G-module H^1(\mathcal{E}_q).

The q-deformed L-function is built from the Frobenius eigenvalues \alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_8 of the local q-zeta function (local q-zeta) acting on H^1(\mathcal{B}), the first étale cohomology of Bring's curve. The elliptic fiber \mathcal{E}_q \hookrightarrow \mathcal{B} is a genus-1 sub-curve. The restriction of Frobenius to H^1(\mathcal{E}_q) \subset H^1(\mathcal{B}) yields a conjugate pair \alpha_{\mathcal{E}}, \bar{\alpha}_{\mathcal{E}} with |\alpha_{\mathcal{E}}| = q^{1/2} (by the Hasse--Weil bound). Define

L(\mathcal{E}_q, s) := \prod_{\mathfrak{m} \in \mathrm{Spec}(R_q)} \frac{1}{1 - \alpha_{\mathcal{E}}(\mathfrak{m}) N(\mathfrak{m})^{-s} + N(\mathfrak{m})^{1-2s}},

where the product runs over maximal ideals of the coordinate ring R_q of Bring's curve, and N(\mathfrak{m}) = q^{f(\mathfrak{m})} is the norm.

The q-Tate--Shafarevich group is the kernel of the local-global map. The fibre functor atlas of the QOU forms a G-gerbe over the spectral base. For each Reeb eigenvalue \rho \in \mathrm{Spec}(\xi_q), let \mathbf{C}_\rho be the localization of \mathbf{C} at \rho (the full subcategory of objects whose spectral support contains \rho). Define

\mathrm{Sha}_q(\mathcal{E}_q) := \ker\!\left( H^1_{\otimes}(\mathbf{C}, E_q) \longrightarrow \prod_{\rho \in \mathrm{Spec}(\xi_q)} H^1_{\otimes}(\mathbf{C}_\rho, E_q) \right),

where H^1_{\otimes} denotes the first cohomology of the monoidal category (classifying torsors under \mathcal{E}_q in \mathbf{C}).
